analysis: Docs-only PR. The visible change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is one added table row at head line 1750. It documents DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS as scheduler tunables read from EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. That row sits in the table of variables that `darkbloom start` copies from the invoking shell into the LaunchAgent plist (LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys). I did not verify whether the Swift passthrough list actually includes these two variables. The same section says other tunables reach the engine only under --foreground or --local, so this row may be inconsistent with the surrounding prose. The inconsistency is a documentation-accuracy concern, not a security regression. The docs/reference/configuration.md hunk (base 393, head 393-395) replaces the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row with a DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK row. Only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied for that file, so I could not read its full text. No code, authentication, attestation, encryption, cache-scope or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The other lines in the supplied cli-reference excerpt are unchanged context. They cover the logout and unenroll flows, the prefix-cache defaults (T-041/SEC-035) and the App Attest worker opt-in. They are not modified, so I make no new claim about them. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the new chunk and step-token environment variables are only performance knobs. They must be bounded in the source, must not widen memory admission or the KV grant, and must not weaken the prefix-cache adoption gates. That source was not supplied. This is a low-priority coverage limit, not a finding.
